source: Compiled on 10 November 2026 from the chronicles named in each war's source; the notes give each town's dates.

wars.name: Gothic War in Italy
towns: Belisarius's first landing in Sicily, summer 535 (Procopius, Wars V.5); approx.
Belisarius entered on the last day of his consulship (Procopius V.5)
The Gothic garrison's last stand in Sicily, taken from the ships' masts (Procopius V.5)
Approx.: the island submitted but for Palermo
Totila's raid on Sicily, 550–551 (Procopius VII.39, VIII.24); approx.
Belisarius crossed from Messina in spring 536; Rhegium fell to Totila in 550 (Procopius VII.37)
Besieged by the Goths 551–552 but held (Procopius VIII.25)
Roscianum surrendered to Totila in 548 (Procopius VII.30)
Bruttium submitted in 536 and fell to Totila in 542; approx.
Held by the Romans throughout; besieged in 544 (Procopius VII.10)
Taken by Belisarius through the aqueduct, November 536; surrendered to Totila in spring 543 (Procopius V.10, VII.7)
The Goths' treasury, held by Aligern until early 553 (Agathias I.20)
Samnium submitted early in 537; Totila razed its walls in 542 (Procopius VII.6)
Compsa, the last Gothic garrison in the south, surrendered in 555
Belisarius entered 9 December 536; Totila took it 17 December 546 and 16 January 550; Narses in summer 552 (Procopius)
Urbs Vetus starved out by Belisarius in 539 (Procopius VI.20)
As Narni; betrayed to Totila in 545 (Procopius VII.12)
Surrendered to Totila after a long siege, about 548 (Procopius VII.35); approx.
Held by Justin in 542 against the Goths; approx.
Narses took it after a three-month siege late in 553 (Agathias I.18)
Taken by John in 538 (Procopius VI.10); held by the Goths when Narses passed in 552 (Procopius VIII.28)
Held by the Romans throughout; relieved after Sena Gallica, 551
Surrendered to Belisarius late in 538 (Procopius VI.19)
Auximum surrendered after a long siege, late 539 (Procopius VI.27)
Vitiges surrendered Ravenna to Belisarius in May 540 (Procopius VI.29)
Totila's victory at Faventia, spring 542 (Procopius VII.4)
Starved into surrender to Totila in 546 (Procopius VII.16)
Went over to the Romans in 538 and was destroyed by the Goths and Burgundians in 539 (Procopius VI.21)
Ticinum, the Goths' last capital, where Teia was raised in 552; approx.
Held by the Goths until 561 or 562
Held by the Goths until 561 or 562
Ildibad's victory over Vitalius near Treviso, 541 (Procopius VII.1)
Sardinia and Corsica, Roman since 534, fell to Totila's fleet in 551 (Procopius VIII.24)
wars.source: Procopius, History of the Wars, books V–VIII; Agathias, Histories

wars.name: Lombard conquest of Italy
towns: Forum Iulii, the Lombards' first duchy (Paul the Deacon II.9)
The patriarch fled to Grado (Paul II.10)
The Isola Comacina held out under Francio until 588 (Paul III.27)
Surrendered after a three-year siege (Paul II.26–27)
Liguria held out until Rothari's conquest of 643
Retaken by the exarch Romanus in 590 (Paul III.31), lost again under Agilulf; approx.
Taken by Agilulf and Ariulf in 592, recovered (Paul IV.8); approx.
The corridor between Rome and Ravenna
The seat of the Lombard dukes of Tuscia; approx.
Sacked by Arichis of Benevento in 596 but held
wars.source: Paul the Deacon, History of the Lombards, books II–IV

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
towns: Tariq ibn Ziyad landed at the rock that bears his name, spring 711
After the battle of Guadalete, 19–26 July 711
The battle near Écija after Guadalete
Taken by Mughith al-Rumi in October 711
The Visigothic capital, taken by Tariq late in 711
Taken by Musa ibn Nusayr after a siege in 712
Musa ibn Nusayr's first conquest in 712
Pelagius's rising; the battle of Covadonga, 718 or 722
Taken by Musa and Tariq in summer 714
Under Agila II and Ardo until about 717
Theodemir's treaty with Abd al-Aziz, 5 April 713
One of the seven towns of the treaty of Tudmir
Taken by al-Samh ibn Malik, 719 or 720
wars.source: The Chronicle of 754; Ibn Abd al-Hakam; al-Maqqari; the treaty of Tudmir

wars.name: Saxon Wars
towns: Taken by Charlemagne in 772, who destroyed the Irminsul nearby; lost and retaken in 776 (Royal Frankish Annals)
Sigiburg, taken in 775 and held in 776 (Annals)
The Karlsburg, built in 776, destroyed in Widukind's rising of 778; approx.
Charlemagne crossed the Weser here in 779; approx.
The battle on the Süntel, 782, a Saxon victory (Annals)
The Eastphalians submitted at the Oker in 775 (Annals)
Charlemagne's camp at the Elbe in 780 was further east; approx.
Charlemagne reached the sea at Hadeln in 797 (Annals)
Nordalbingia, cleared and given to the Obotrites in 804
The Obotrites, Charlemagne's allies, beat the Nordalbingians at Bornhöved in 798 (Annals)
The Frankish stronghold (Büraburg), attacked by the Saxons in 774
A trading post on the Elbe from 805; approx.
wars.source: The Royal Frankish Annals; Einhard, Life of Charlemagne

wars.name: Great Heathen Army in England
towns: The army wintered in East Anglia in 865–866, and returned in 869, when Edmund was killed (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle)
Guthrum's army wintered at Cambridge in 874–875 (Chronicle)
Taken on All Saints' Day, 866; the Northumbrian kings died attacking it on 21 March 867 (Chronicle)
Bernicia, under English rulers at Bamburgh
Halfdan's raids on Strathclyde and Cumbria, 875; approx.
Besieged by Mercia and Wessex in 868; the army returned to York (Chronicle)
Lindsey: the army wintered at Torksey in 872–873
The army drove Burgred out from Repton in 874 (Chronicle)
Mercia under Ceolwulf II, the army's client from 874; parted in 877
The army wintered in London in 871–872 (Chronicle)
The army's camp in the campaign of 871 (Chronicle)
Wessex overrun after Twelfth Night 878; approx.
The army went from Wareham to Exeter (Chronicle, 877)
Taken at Twelfth Night 878; surrendered after Edington, May 878 (Chronicle)
wars.source: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle; Asser, Life of King Alfred

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
towns: Asad ibn al-Furat landed at Mazara on 17 June 827
Surrendered after a year's siege, September 831
Castrogiovanni, entered through a drain on 24 January 859
Stormed on 21 May 878 after a nine-month siege
Taken by Ibrahim II on 1 August 902
The Val Demone's Christian strongholds; approx.
wars.source: Ibn al-Athir; the Cambridge Chronicle; Theophanes Continuatus

wars.name: Norman conquest of England
towns: William landed at Pevensey on 28 September and moved to Hastings (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D; William of Poitiers)
Taken a week after the battle of 14 October (William of Poitiers)
Submitted on the march from Dover (William of Poitiers)
Queen Edith's city submitted in November (William of Poitiers)
William crossed the Thames at Wallingford, where Archbishop Stigand submitted (William of Poitiers)
The English leaders submitted at Berkhamsted (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D)
Entered before the coronation of 25 December (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D)
William fitzOsbern held Hereford from 1067 (Orderic Vitalis)
Surrendered after an eighteen-day siege early in 1068 (Orderic Vitalis)
Castle built on the northern campaign of summer 1068 (Orderic Vitalis)
Castle built on the return from York in 1068 (Orderic Vitalis)
Sacked by Hereward and the Danes on 2 June 1070, then held by Abbot Turold (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle E)
First taken in 1068; lost to the English and Danes on 21 September 1069; retaken before Christmas (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D)
Robert de Comines was killed in Durham on 28 January 1069; the harrying reached the Tees early in 1070 (Symeon of Durham)
Taken at the end of the harrying, early in 1070 (Orderic Vitalis)
Approx.; the rebels of Staffordshire were put down in 1070
Approx.; besieged by Eadric the Wild and the Welsh in 1069 (Orderic Vitalis)
Held by Hereward and Morcar from 1070 until William took the isle in 1071 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle D and E)
wars.source: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (D and E); William of Poitiers; Orderic Vitalis; Symeon of Durham; Huscroft, The Norman Conquest (2009)

wars.name: First Crusade
towns: Alexios I's capital, where the armies gathered in 1096 and 1097
Byzantine before the armies came (Anna Komnene)
Surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June 1097 (Anna Komnene; Gesta Francorum)
The battle of 1 July 1097 left the town Turkish
Taken by John Doukas in the summer of 1097 (Anna Komnene)
Approx.; John Doukas reached Polybotus in 1098 (Anna Komnene)
Armenian; the armies passed in October 1097
Taken by Baldwin and Tancred in September 1097 (Fulcher of Chartres)
Bought by Baldwin from its emir Balduk (Fulcher of Chartres)
Baldwin succeeded Thoros on 10 March 1098 (Fulcher of Chartres)
Taken on 3 June 1098 after an eight-month siege (Gesta Francorum)
Approx.; held for Byzantium from late 1098
The Banu Ammar's; the armies besieged Arqa nearby from February to May 1099
Abandoned by the Fatimids; a Genoese fleet put in in June 1099 (Raymond of Aguilers)
Taken from the Artuqids by the Fatimids in August 1098; stormed on 15 July 1099 (Gesta Francorum)
Approx.; submitted to Tancred and Eustace after Jerusalem fell
Fatimid after the battle of 12 August 1099
wars.source: Gesta Francorum; Fulcher of Chartres; Raymond of Aguilers; Anna Komnene, Alexiad; Riley-Smith, The First Crusade and the Idea of Crusading (1986); Asbridge, The First Crusade (2004)

wars.name: Castile's conquest of Toledo
towns: Taken by Alfonso VI in 1079 (Chronicle of Pelayo of Oviedo)
Surrendered on 25 May 1085 (Anales Toledanos; Ibn Bassam)
Approx.; with the dowry of Zaida, Alfonso's Muslim consort
The Aftasids' capital; Sagrajas was fought nearby on 23 October 1086
Approx.; al-Qadir ruled it as Alfonso's client from 1086 until he was killed in October 1092
wars.source: Anales Toledanos; Ibn Bassam; Ibn Idhari; Reilly, The Kingdom of León-Castilla under King Alfonso VI (1988)
